mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week collapse in WORKPLACES mobility (from -13.7 to -42.4) removes commute-linked foot traffic that normally feeds retail corridors, so RETAIL_REC will average lower over the next four weeks than the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -13.7 to -42.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is equal to or higher than its 28-day trailing mean despite the WORKPLACES collapse, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A transit mobility decline exceeding 10 points week-on-week signals newly imposed mobility restrictions or public transit curtailment, which mechanically suppresses discretionary retail and recreation trips over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -15.3 to -28.1, a 12.8 point week-on-week drop
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean does not fall relative to the trigger week despite the >10pt TRANSIT drop, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp declines in WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM in the same week indicate a coordinated behavioral retreat from all non-essential and essential in-person errands, compounding to depress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM drop more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 28.7 points and GROCERY_PHARM fell 15.8 points in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward decline is no larger than the decline predicted by WORKPLACES alone (i.e., no compounding effect observed), the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility alongside a steep WORKPLACES decline indicates an active stay-at-home policy regime, under which RETAIL_REC will continue to decline over the next four weeks as the regime persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 3.1 while WORKPLACES fell to -42.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean exceeds its 28-day trailing mean while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and WORKPLACES remains depressed, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained multi-week improvement in PARKS mobility (from -33.0 to +1.7) reflects a seasonal shift toward outdoor activity that is associated with broader community re-engagement in local commerce, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose steadily from -33.0 to +1.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is lower than its trailing mean despite PARKS maintaining a positive or improving trend, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An abrupt drop in GROCERY_PHARM mobility of more than 10 points in a single week, after several weeks of stability near baseline, signals a new restriction on even essential in-person shopping, predicting an immediate one-week decline in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 10 points week-on-week after being near zero
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 1.9 to -13.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following the GROCERY_PHARM threshold breach, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint occurrence of rising RESIDENTIAL mobility and falling TRANSIT mobility in the same week indicates a behavioral shift toward home confinement and avoidance of shared transit, which together predict an immediate one-week suppression of RETAIL_REC beyond what either series alone implies.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week while TRANSIT falls more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 3.1 while TRANSIT fell by 12.8 points in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's one-week forward value does not fall below the trigger-week value when both conditions co-occur, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where WORKPLACES has just suffered an unprecedented single-week shock exceeding 25 points, commuting-linked retail spillover collapses abruptly, producing a sharp two-week downturn in RETAIL_REC before any stabilization occurs.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 25 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 28.7 points week-on-week, the largest move in the series
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean is flat or higher than its trailing mean despite the >25-point WORKPLACES shock, the hypothesis is rejected.
